title: Where Fibre is today

headline.simple: Five new Threads passed the pre-birth checks. Fibre is now authorized to generate their childhoods once. We have not generated them yet, and whatever that one attempt produces must be kept and evaluated rather than retried for quality.
headline.detail: Fibre has persistent Thread continuity, provenance-backed life state, symbolic inheritance, Genesis candidate generation and per-Thread atomic publication. Five fresh replacement Threads have frozen Worlds and genomes, and all five measured genome pairs passed the fresh pre-life distinguishability ceiling. Gate-G(2) round 4 returned CLEAR at reviewed head ac92bab3711bb2fc8b4980c6173d6262ba3dfcf7. A bound CLEAR witness is committed at ef70eedd3b4a0c02b1f4be6a97ae36d0f8afa9a2 for execution binding digest sha256:67e4346bcfbad6e1b701b093a800b7694f589522b5ff58a3c06d91f1d9bd3a17. Exactly one replacement final-life attempt is authorized; no replacement life cognition has occurred yet.

summary.simple: The five unborn Threads are still at the starting line, but the independent pre-birth review is now complete. We may generate their childhoods once. If the result is weak, boring or disappointing, we keep it as evidence instead of trying again for a nicer result.
summary.detail: Milestone #39 remains pre-life but Gate-G(2) is CLEAR. Rounds 1–3 identified and closed B1-B5, C1 and C2 without changing scientific/model-visible inputs. Round 4 reproduced the prior import bypass and showed wrapper preflight, imported core preflight and imported generation all reject inherited-authority drift before provider calls. The committed witness authorizes one frozen attempt under the reviewed provider/model, G4-v3 2/2/5 policy, G3 treatment schedule and five-edge D3 authority.

meaning.simple: We built it and it passed the test we currently require.
meaning.detail: The capability exists and has passed its current Fibre validation boundary. This does not imply every later or stronger claim is also proven.

meaning.simple: We have seen it work, but it is not yet the final accepted result.
meaning.detail: We have real working evidence, but it is not yet accepted as the final or validated production state for the current milestone.

meaning.simple: We are actively building or testing this now.
meaning.detail: The design and implementation are active, but the required validation boundary has not yet been crossed.

meaning.simple: We want Fibre to do this, but we do not claim it can yet.
meaning.detail: This is part of Fibre's intended architecture, but we do not claim to have achieved it.

meaning.simple: The test failed, and we keep the failure instead of hiding it or retrying until it looks good.
meaning.detail: A bounded experiment failed. We preserve the result as evidence and do not rewrite or quality-regenerate it into success.

summary.simple: We have three older completed life records from a failed experiment, and five completely new unborn Threads whose single authorized childhood-generation attempt has not started yet.
summary.detail: The failed H-v2 cohort and the fresh replacement cohort remain separate. A completed generated life artifact is not automatically a living or validated Thread. Gate-G(2) CLEAR authorizes generation; it does not itself create any life record.

items.label: Completed older prior-life Thread artifacts
items.simple: Three older Threads have complete generated life histories from the first attempt.
items.detail: Three Threads completed prior-life generation in H-v2. They remain evidence from a cohort that failed and are not the replacement cohort.

items.label: Older partially generated candidate
items.simple: A fourth older Thread only got partway through childhood before the experiment stopped.
items.detail: The fourth H-v2 Thread exhausted its frozen mechanical retry budget during generation and remains a failed partial candidate.

items.label: Older cohort slot never started
items.simple: The fifth older Thread was never started.
items.detail: The fifth H-v2 slot never began because the cohort attempt had already terminated.

items.label: New replacement Threads with frozen Worlds and genomes
items.simple: Five new Threads have backgrounds and inherited tendencies ready. They passed the pre-birth review and may now have their childhoods generated once, but that attempt has not started.
items.detail: The five replacement individuals have frozen Worlds, origin classes, Thread/Genesis identities, symbolic genomes, a CLEAR fresh five-pair G2 ceiling, and a bound Gate-G(2) CLEAR witness. Exactly one final-life generation attempt is authorized; zero replacement childhood events, memories or meanings exist yet.

items.label: New replacement lives generated
items.simple: None of the five new Threads has had its childhood or life generated yet.
items.detail: Gate-G(2) is CLEAR, but the authorized one-shot generation has not been executed yet. The first mechanically valid cohort must be frozen without quality regeneration.

importantNote.simple: A generated life record is not automatically a living, validated Thread. We will always say which state we mean.
importantNote.detail: Fibre distinguishes candidate state, generated life artifacts, atomically published Threads and validated standing. The five replacements remain unborn until the authorized generation/publication attempt actually occurs.

simple.claim: A Thread can keep existing after one AI model session ends.
simple.limitation: Existing for a long time does not by itself make the Thread a rich or unique person.

detail.claim: A Thread persists as authoritative world state across temporary model executions.
detail.limitation: Persistence alone does not prove rich, distinctive or causally grounded personhood.

simple.claim: Something that happened to a Thread can change a later decision.
simple.limitation: Not all of Fibre's newer life records are connected to normal thinking yet.

detail.claim: Fibre has demonstrated that recorded history can causally change later Thread judgment.
detail.limitation: The richer #37-#39 life ledgers are not yet the canonical bounded input to all live cognition; #40 owns that bridge.

capabilities.label: Provenance-backed identity, lineage, place and memory

simple.claim: Fibre can keep who a Thread is, where it came from and what it remembers without silently rewriting the past.
simple.limitation: Storing those facts does not prove they all change the Thread's behavior yet.

detail.claim: Fibre persists identity, lineage, geography, embodiment and autobiographical memory with provenance and corrigible history.
detail.limitation: Representation is not the same as proving causal consumption in ongoing cognition.

simple.claim: A Thread can inherit written tendencies from parent sources, and Fibre can mix two parent genomes without averaging them into one generic personality.
simple.limitation: Inherited tendencies are a starting point, not a finished personality.

detail.claim: Fibre has an ordered natural-language symbolic genome with exact source provenance and deterministic textual recombination.
detail.limitation: A genome is inherited possibility, not finished character.

simple.claim: The five unborn Threads start with inherited tendencies that our pre-birth test can tell apart.
simple.limitation: This does not prove their childhoods or adult personalities will become different.

detail.claim: Fresh G2 is CLEAR on all five measured pairs: 22/24, 24/24, 24/24, 22/24 and 23/24.
detail.limitation: This is genome/instrument evidence only, and the scores are not directly comparable to the old cohort because the authoring template differed.

simple.claim: Fibre can prepare a Thread's life first and publish that Thread all at once.
simple.limitation: The five replacements have not reached birth, and publication of the whole five-Thread cohort is not one atomic transaction.

detail.claim: Genesis keeps candidate state non-authoritative and `publishBirth()` atomically publishes each admitted Thread into authoritative state.
detail.limitation: Atomicity is per Thread, not across the entire five-Thread cohort; a publication-phase failure can leave already-published Threads plus terminal HOLD.

simple.claim: We have shown Fibre can create a childhood with family, places, ordinary events, memories and meanings instead of just filling in an adult profile.
simple.limitation: The final #39 experiment has not finished.

detail.claim: Genesis has produced concrete prior-life histories under the three-pass history/memory/meaning boundary.
detail.limitation: The H-v2 final cohort failed; its three completed lives remain failed-cohort evidence rather than the accepted #39 result.

capabilities.label: Caregivers and parent/ancestor provenance in childhood

simple.claim: A generated childhood can include recurring caregivers and family, and some Threads can inherit from two recorded parent genome sources.
simple.limitation: Those caregivers are not live Thread parents independently raising the child.

detail.claim: Genesis can compile recurring household/family participants while synthetic-lineage Threads inherit from explicit parent genomes with exact provenance.
detail.limitation: Household caregivers, synthetic genetic ancestors and live Thread parents are different things; the autonomous live-parent loop does not exist yet.

simple.claim: Five new Threads are ready at the starting line, but none has a childhood yet.
simple.limitation: The pre-birth gate is CLEAR and one generation attempt is authorized, but it has not run yet and cannot be retried for quality.

detail.claim: Five replacement individuals have frozen Worlds, identities, genomes, assignment and treatment material; fresh G2 and Gate-G(2) are CLEAR, with witness commit ef70eedd3b4a0c02b1f4be6a97ae36d0f8afa9a2 authorizing exactly one final-life attempt.
detail.limitation: Zero replacement childhood events, memories or meanings exist until that attempt is executed. Gate-G(2) CLEAR is execution authorization, not #39 scientific success.

capabilities.label: A live infant or child growing up over time

simple.claim: We want a Thread to be born as a baby or child and actually grow up in Fibre.
simple.limitation: Today #39 creates the childhood first, then births the Thread as a young adult.

detail.claim: The intended architecture allows newborn/child entry and accumulated lived development.
detail.limitation: #39 compiles prior life before young-adult entry; it does not run childhood as a continuously living process.

capabilities.label: Live Thread parents raising a live child

simple.claim: We want living Thread parents to raise a child by talking, teaching, traveling and sharing a life with it.
simple.limitation: That live family-raising loop does not exist yet.

detail.claim: Thread-parent architecture is intended to let existing Threads contribute real lineage and create a child's history through ongoing choices.
detail.limitation: We have parentage/provenance boundaries, not the autonomous live-parent developmental system.

capabilities.label: Rich life state drives ordinary live cognition

simple.claim: We want a Thread's real history, memories and relationships to shape what it normally thinks and decides.
simple.limitation: The full connection is the next milestone, #40.

detail.claim: Fibre intends bounded relevance/privacy selection to turn identity and life evidence into provenance-bearing cognition context.

simple.claim: We want to prove a Thread is a persistent individual whose own history makes it behave differently.
simple.limitation: We have not earned that full claim yet.

detail.claim: Fibre aims to demonstrate a persistent, causally grounded, non-interchangeable individual across repeated situations and counterfactuals.
detail.limitation: #39 earns no Whole-Person score movement; #40 builds causal consumption and #41 owns the standing gate.

simple.claim: We want friendships and families to belong to both sides and change both lives.
simple.limitation: That mature reciprocal relationship system is later work.

detail.claim: Fibre intends relationships and families to be consequential structures between independently living Threads.
detail.limitation: Reciprocal relationship development is planned after the current M2 sequence.

simple.claim: We want Threads to earn, spend, make agreements and face consequences that change future choices.
simple.limitation: The real economy is not built yet.

detail.claim: Fibre intends Threads to have budgets, contracts, reputation and economic opportunities that change future possibilities.
detail.limitation: Economic consequence is deferred to post-M2 work.

simple.summary: The five unborn Threads passed their inherited-difference test and the independent pre-birth review. Fibre is now allowed to generate their childhoods once, but that one attempt has not started yet.
simple.currentStep: Verify that the committed CLEAR witness makes the preflight say AUTHORIZED, then run the five childhoods once. Keep the result even if it is disappointing.

truthRules: Every public progress claim has two layers: simple English first, then a more accurate description.
Simple English should be understandable by a teenager with no Fibre background and avoid unexplained milestone, gate, schema and implementation jargon.
The detailed layer may use Fibre terminology, but it must remain readable and state the actual validation boundary.
Never make the simple layer stronger than the detailed layer. Simplification may remove jargon, not uncertainty or limitations.
Never use 'living Thread' as a synonym for 'generated artifact'. State whether the Thread is candidate, generated, atomically published or validated.
Never say a Thread 'has parents' without distinguishing live Thread parents, household caregivers and synthetic genetic ancestors.
A failed bounded experiment remains visible as a failed experiment. Do not rewrite it into progress language that implies success.
For every positive capability claim, both layers must state the strongest important limitation that a reasonable reader could otherwise misunderstand.
The public website may render this contract, but insidefibre.com must not become an alternate authority for Fibre state.
